content: On AMD Strix Halo APUs, the GPU can only access a configurable slice of the total LPDDR5X pool (up to ~96 GB on the top SKU), so a low allocation directly caps the size of AI models, textures, or frame buffers the GPU can hold. Because the CPU and GPU draw from the same physical memory, a large GPU carve-out starves the OS and CPU of available RAM, risking system-wide slowdowns or out-of-memory failures. Finally, the shared memory bandwidth is fixed regardless of how the pool is divided, so allocating more memory to the GPU increases capacity without increasing throughput, which can create a bandwidth bottleneck that limits real-world performance.
